entries.definition: being very thin
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Thin and rough-looking, with nothing graceful about it.

entries.definition: slow to learn or understand; lacking intellectual acuity
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal reproach - slow to understand, and perhaps unwilling to.
examples: he was either normally stupid or being deliberately obtuse

entries.definition: exceptionally bad or displeasing
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Moral revulsion - condemns rather than criticises.

entries.definition: in disarray; extremely disorderly
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The gentlest word here - rumpled clothes are forgiven, and sometimes liked.

entries.definition: (used informally especially for emphasis) real or genuine
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Homely and regional; the emphasis of someone who expects to be doubted.
examples: went upriver to look at a sure-enough fish wheel

entries.definition: marked by refinement in taste and manners
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The plain positive of the group: it describes conduct anyone can manage, and asks for no admiration.

entries.definition: steadfast in allegiance or duty
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The plain word and the strongest, because it needs no institution to make sense.

entries.definition: marked by deliberate deceptiveness especially by pretending one set of feelings and acting under the influence of another
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts the intent in view: not merely wrong, but meaning to mislead.
examples: she was a deceitful scheming little thing

entries.definition: having or showing a tender and considerate and helpful nature; used especially of persons and their behavior
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The plain, unshowy word, and the one people most want said about them.

entries.definition: in a misleading way
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *misleading*: stops short of accusation: it reports the effect, and leaves the intent unstated.

entries.definition: marked by anger or resentment or hostility
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Of a mood rather than an outburst - settled, silent and unpleasant to be near.

entries.definition: unwilling to spend (money, time, resources, etc.)
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names the missing virtue rather than the present vice, which makes it the politer complaint.
examples: an ungenerous response to the appeal for funds

entries.definition: thickly covered with ingrained dirt or soot
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: This dirt sense is dated; a modern reader will hear the sexual one first.

entries.definition: cheerful and bright
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The cheer has reached the face and is impossible to miss.

entries.definition: (used of metals) consisting of or alloyed with inferior metal
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Of metals, where it is technical. The moral sense is a separate and much older word.

entries.definition: dead
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The most consoling form - reframes death as rest and the end of suffering.
examples: After a long illness, he is at peace.

entries.definition: in a domineering high-handed manner
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *high-handed*: about a single act more often than a character - a decision taken over someone's head.
examples: he behaved high-handedly toward his employees

entries.definition: rebuke formally
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Rare and legalistic; it frames the fault as very nearly a crime.

entries.definition: resembling an owl; solemn and wise in appearance
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Appearance only. The owl looks wise; that is the whole of its claim.

entries.definition: (used colloquially) having the relationship of friends or pals
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Openly mocking - the reduplication does the sneering for you.

entries.definition: exhibiting childlike simplicity and credulity
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Warm. It keeps the simplicity and drops the accusation.

entries.definition: carefree and happy and lighthearted
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Carefree. The same word covers a happy lightness and a failure to take something seriously.
examples: was loved for her blithe spirit

entries.definition: poor enough to need help from others
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Frames poverty as requiring help; of a person's temperament it means something else entirely.

entries.definition: obstinate and stupid
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Adds stupidity to the charge - not just unmoving but unable to see why it should move.

entries.definition: tenaciously unwilling or marked by tenacious unwillingness to yield
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Mildly critical, and often affectionate - it can be said of a child or a stain.
examples: He was too stubborn to apologize.

entries.definition: lacking excess flesh
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plain, unloaded word - it states the shape and passes no judgement.
examples: you can't be too rich or too thin

entries.definition: lacking even the rudiments of courage; abjectly fearful
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Abject cowardice - formal and thoroughly contemptuous.
examples: the craven fellow turned and ran
a craven proposal to raise the white flag

entries.definition: owing or owed feudal allegiance and service
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Feudal and historical: allegiance owed by rank, not chosen.

entries.definition: without compunction or human feeling
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Premeditation is the whole charge - the harm was planned while calm.

entries.definition: offensively self-assured or given to exercising usually unwarranted power
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: It allows no reply, which is the whole of the offence.

entries.definition: bad; unfortunate
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal censure, expecting the reader to share the judgement.
examples: my finances were in a deplorable state

entries.definition: resembling swine; coarsely gluttonous or greedy
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Broader than eating: it condemns the whole manner of the person.

entries.definition: obstreperous
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: British; it makes the defiance sound adolescent, which is the insult.

entries.definition: of very poor quality; flimsy
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Specific to sound, and precise enough to be almost neutral.

entries.definition: in a proud and domineering manner
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *cavalier*: disregard worn lightly, as though the other person's stake were not real.

entries.definition: thickly covered with ingrained dirt or soot
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Mild enough to be affectionate about a child, and mildly damning about a motive.

entries.definition: cry weakly or softly
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Long and loud with grief - dramatic, and taken seriously.

entries.definition: obstinate and stupid
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The same accusation with a harder image; rare, and unkind about the head as well.

entries.definition: believing the worst of human nature and motives; having a sneering disbelief in e.g. selflessness of others
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The longer form of the same judgement, and rarer.

entries.definition: unpleasant to look at
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Offends the eye - used more comfortably of things than of people.

entries.definition: lacking refinement or cultivation or taste
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: About texture originally, and it still suggests something unfinished.
examples: he had coarse manners but a first-rate mind

entries.definition: given to haughty disregard of others
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Disregard worn lightly, as though the other person's stake were not real.

entries.definition: at an advanced stage of erosion (pronounced as one syllable)
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The geological sense - a landscape at an advanced stage of erosion.

entries.definition: in fortunate circumstances financially; moderately rich
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The modest way to say it - enough money, and no wish to discuss it.
examples: they were comfortable or even wealthy by some standards

entries.definition: deceptive or fraudulent; disposed to cheat or defraud or deceive
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain word for it, and still an accusation - it names a settled disposition to cheat, not one bad day.

entries.definition: having or showing great eagerness or enthusiasm
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Enthusiasm at temperature: the wanting is hot rather than steady.

entries.definition: take to task
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: A mild, old-fashioned rebuke - correction rather than attack.

entries.definition: (used colloquially) overly conceited or arrogant
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Crude and dismissive - looking down on people and showing it.
examples: a snotty little scion of a degenerate family
a snotty remark about where we live
